source: tor 0.4.7.13 on a local chutney hs-v3 network, 2026-08-05
how: The service's identity key is net/nodes/009h/hidden_service/hs_ed25519_public_key (bytes 32..64, after the 32-byte 'ed25519v1-public: type0' tag). The blinded key is extension type 4 ('signed-with-ed25519-key') of the descriptor-signing-key-cert in the descriptor tor itself fetched, read back with 'GETINFO hs/client/desc/id/<addr>' on the client's control port. So both values are tor's, produced by tor, and neither passed through any code of ours.
why: A blinded key is the one input a client cannot check locally: get it wrong and the HSDir simply answers 404, which is indistinguishable from a service that is not published. It needs an external vector or it has no oracle at all.

network.note: fresh-until minus valid-after from the live consensus. chutney votes every 20s; the real network every hour.
network.periodLengthNote: SHARED_RANDOM_N_ROUNDS * SHARED_RANDOM_N_PHASES * votingInterval / 60 = 24*20/60. NOT hsdir_interval's 1440 default: tor's get_time_period_length() ignores the consensus parameter entirely when TestingTorNetwork is set.
network.rotationOffsetNote: SHARED_RANDOM_N_ROUNDS * votingInterval / 60 = 12*20/60. rend-spec-v3's '720 minutes' is only right when a voting period is an hour.

addressExamplesNote: Verbatim from rend-spec-v3 section 6, 'Here are a few example addresses'. Each must decode and its checksum must be the one we compute, so they test the encoding against the specification's own output rather than against ours.
invalidExamplesNote: From rend-spec-v3 section 1.2, where the prose is 'a new name following this specification might look like' — it is illustrative and its checksum does NOT validate. Found by including it among the valid examples and having it fail. Kept as a negative case, which is worth more than dropping it: it is a real 56-character v3-shaped address with a wrong checksum, which is exactly what a mistyped one is.
